topics.description: Soviet leader who succeeded Joseph Stalin, denounced Stalinist repression in the 1956 Secret Speech, and led the USSR during major Cold War events including the Cuban Missile Crisis.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This man's 1957 visit to the Turkish embassy in his country ended a summer crisis over military  influence in Syria. This leader, who launched the failed Virgin Lands Campaign, left the Four  Powers Summit after only a day due to tensions over the (*) U-2 incident. The satellite Sputnik was  launched under this leader, with whom Fidel Castro struck a deal to place nuclear missiles in Cuba. This  leader's “Secret Speech” denounced the repression of the Stalin era. For 10 points, name this Soviet  politician who bested Georgy Malenkov in a 1950s leadership struggle.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man’s Doctor’s Plot involved accusing a group of Jewish doctors in Moscow of plotting to assassinate Soviet leaders. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this leader who aided a campaign of political repression and genocide known as the Great Purge. This leader, who organized his country’s economy into five-year plans, was the Soviet leader during World War II.
parts.answer: Joseph Vissarionovich Stalin [accept Ioseb Besarionis dzе Jugashvili]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] After Stalin’s death, this successor of his denounced him in a “Secret Speech” called “On the Cult of Personality and Its Consequences.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Kruschev and Stalin were both members of the Soviet party espousing this ideology. This ideology is structured around common ownership of the means of production, and was named after a manifesto written by Karl Marx.

topics.description: Roman general and politician who was a member of the Second Triumvirate and allied with Cleopatra VII.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Clodius Pulcher allegedly dressed as a woman to seduce this man’s wife while he was Pontifex Maximus.  This man’s daughter, Julia, died in childbirth while married to a man who formed the Second Triumvirate  with his (*) adopted son. This man may have fathered one of the men who stabbed him on the Senate floor, Marcus  Junius Brutus. For 10 points, Cleopatra had a relationship with what man, who was assassinated on the Ides of  March?

topics.description: The short-lived Chinese imperial dynasty that unified China under Qin Shi Huang and promoted Legalism and major early construction of the Great Wall.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One ruler of this modern-day country had his dead body concealed in a fish cart so his chancellor could forge his will. This country adopted Legalism and book-burning under a ruler who was buried with the (*) Terracotta Army. This country was first unified by Shi Huangdi, whose dynasty was overthrown by the Han. For 10 points, name this country, whose Qin dynasty began construction of the Great Wall.
parts.answer: China [or Zhongguo; prompt on Qin dynasty before mention]

topics.description: The Chinese imperial dynasty that ruled from 1368 to 1644, sponsored Zheng He’s voyages, and preceded the Qing dynasty.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Parakramabahu VI rose to power after this dynasty defeated the Kotte kingdom. This dynasty’s last emperor was found hanging from a tree in Jingshan Park. A giraffe from Malindi was considered a Mandate of Heaven during this dynasty, whose Emperor Yingzong was captured by Esan Taishi in the Tumu Crisis. This dynasty’s first leader won the Battle of Lake Poyang as a commander of the (*) Red Turbans. Seven treasure voyages led by Zheng He [jung HUH] were conducted during this dynasty. In this dynasty, Nanjing was replaced as the capital by the Forbidden City in Beijing. For 10 points, name this dynasty that was succeeded by the Qing.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In his pseudo-historical book 1421, Gavin Menzies claimed that an explorer from this dynasty visited the Americas before Christopher Columbus. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Chinese dynasty, renowned for its blue and white porcelain, which succeeded the Yuan dynasty and preceded the Qing dynasty.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The aforementioned explorer, Zheng He, brought exotic animals to China from the East African coast with this name. The Bantu language of this name is the most widely spoken in Africa.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Zheng He made his massive voyages using junks, a type of this vessel. Lateen sails helped merchants and sailors cross the Indian Ocean in these vessels during monsoon season.

topics.description: An 1862 speech by Otto von Bismarck arguing that German unification and major political questions would be decided by military power and practical politics rather than parliamentary speeches and majority decisions.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This leader was nicknamed the “Iron Chancellor” for conducting diplomacy using the strategy of Realpolitik. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Prussian statesman, who masterminded the Unification of Germany.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Two answers required. In a speech arguing for an increase in military spending, Bismarck proclaimed that the “great questions of the day [would] be decided” by these two substances, which title the speech. Name both.
parts.answer: blood and iron [accept “Blood and Iron” Speech; DO NOT PROMPT ON PARTIAL ANSWERS]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Bismarck correctly predicted this conflict by saying that trouble in the Balkans would set off a major European war. This conflict was sparked by the assassination of Franz Ferdinand in 1914.
parts.answer: World War I [or WWI or the Great War]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This address states that the title substances, not “speeches and majority decisions,” will decide “the  great questions of the day.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Identify this 1862 speech about German unification.
parts.answer: ANSWER: “Blood and Iron” speech [or Blut und Eisen]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] The “Blood and Iron” speech was given by this “Iron Chancellor” of the German Empire from 1871  to 1890, who promoted Realpolitik (ray-AHL-pah-lit-EEK).

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The “Blood and Iron” speech cites the “great mistake” of a series of pan-German revolutions that  began in this year, which was known as the Springtime of the Peoples.

topics.description: Spanish conquistador who led the conquest of the Inca Empire and captured Atahualpa.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A remnant of this empire survived until Tupac Amaru’s execution following the Battle of Vilcabamba. This empire employed chasqui messengers to run its road system, carrying knotted quipu. Huascar lost a civil war to a ruler of this empire, who was forced to fill a room with (*) silver by Francisco Pizarro. Atahualpa was a ruler of this empire. For 10 points, name these builders of Machu Picchu, an empire centered on Cuzco in modern-day Peru.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This empire's last effective ruler unsuccessfully offered his captors a room full of gold in exchange for his freedom. Chasqui runners carried knotted string messages called quipu along this empire’s extensive network of roads. This empire’s ruler Atahualpa was killed during this empire’s conquest by (*) Francisco Pizarro. Cities like Cusco and Machu Picchu were a part of, for 10 points, what South American empire centered on Peru?

topics.description: The ancient city in northwestern Anatolia traditionally associated with the Trojan War and identified with the archaeological site of Hisarlik in modern Turkey.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In this modern-day country, the seventh of an ancient city’s nine layers shows scorch marks consistent with a foreign siege. The neolithic cities of Catalhoyuk and Gobekli Tepe are located in this country, where Heinrich Schliemann excavated the site of ancient (*) Troy. This country was home to the capital of the Eastern Roman Empire. For 10 points, name this modern-day country once called “Asia Minor,” where the Hittites complained about people from Constantinople.
parts.answer: Turkey [or the Republic of Turkey; or Turkiye Cumhuriyeti]

parts.label: L
parts.question: A thirty-meter-high mound at a site where this city likely stood was excavated by Frank Calvert. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this ancient city, likely corresponding to the modern site of Hisarlik (HISS-ar-lik) near the Aegean (uh-JEE-un) Sea.
parts.answer: Troy [or Troia; or Ilium; or Ilion]

parts.label: B
parts.question: The site of Hisarlik was excavated in this country, whose other archaeological site of Çatalhüyük (chaa-TAHL-HOO-yook) was a proto-city in the region of Anatolia (AN-uh-TOL-ee-uh).
parts.answer: Turkey [or Republic of Türkiye; or Turkey Cumhuriyeti]

parts.label: C
parts.question: After Calvert, Hisarlik was excavated by this German archaeologist who also excavated Mycenae (mai-SEE-nee) and Tiryns (TEER-inz). He smuggled out a collection of artifacts from Hisarlik called Priam's Treasure.

topics.description: The historical process and goal of legally ending chattel slavery, including major emancipations in Brazil, the United States, Britain, and elsewhere.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Saraiva-Cotegipe Law and the Rio Branco Law began this process in one country. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this process completed by the Golden Law in that country. The U.S. completed this process by passing the 13th Amendment. A description is acceptable.
parts.answer: abolishing slavery [or ending slavery; prompt on abolition with “what was abolished?”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Golden Law was passed in this largest South American country, the only one with Portuguese as its official language.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The Golden Law was passed by a monarch with this name. Two monarchs with this name ruled Brazil immediately after its independence from Portugal.
parts.answer: Pedro [accept Dom Pedro I or Dom Pedro II]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Thomas Clarkson published a list of people who supported this goal, including its “godfather,” Granville Sharp. Isabel the Redemptress accomplished this goal with a law that succeeded the Rio Branco Law. Supporters of this goal grew after the case Somerset v. Stewart, and wore medallions of a kneeling man created by Josiah Wedgwood. The Saints organized Royal Navy blockades in support of this goal while led by William (*) Wilberforce. While Pedro II [“the second”] was in Europe, this goal was accomplished by Brazil’s Golden Law. For 10 points, name this goal accomplished in the U.S. with the Thirteenth Amendment and the Emancipation Proclamation.
parts.answer: abolition of slavery [accept word forms indicating ending slavery; prompt on abolition with “Of what?”]

topics.description: Organized armed conflict among political communities, states, groups, or other organized communities.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The Kahama chimpanzee community was disbanded after chimpanzees in Gombe National Park engaged in this activity, which was documented by Jane Goodall. The Chinese strategist Sun Tzu wrote a book about the (*) "Art" of this activity. The Geneva Convention established laws governing, for 10 points, what activity in which large groups or nations engage in armed conflict?
parts.answer: war [or warfare; accept synonyms such as fighting, combat, violence, etc. until “Art” is read and prompt afterwards; accept The Art of War; accept the Gombe Chimpanzee War]

topics.description: A country in the Middle East and Levant on the eastern Mediterranean, established in 1948 and central to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Cases 1000 and 2000 are corruption and bribery cases brought against a leader in this country. A party in this country founded in 2019 which is led by a former army chief of staff is named after the colors of this country's flag. Another party in this country which is led by Mansour Abbas and holds only four seats in the legislature was the last to join a 2021 electoral coalition. In 2021, (*) Naftali Bennett was sworn in as this country’s prime minister in the fourth election in two years. This country’s parliament, the Knesset, was long controlled by the Likud party. For 10 points, name this country which was led from 2009 to 2021 by Benjamin Netanyahu.
parts.answer: Israel [or State of Israel or Medinat Yisra’el]
